rules.title: Structural type identity is layout-stable, name-independent
rules.statement: A type's structural identity (used for wire/persistent identity) is computed by a tag-prefixed structural walk that bears no struct/field NAME: two types with identical physical layout (same primitive leaves, same field types in order, same array sizes) have equal identity regardless of struct/field renames. Each primitive kind has a distinct code; aggregate shapes carry distinct shape tags (struct/tuple/array/ptr/&/&mut/slice/enum/fnptr/void/wstatic).
rules.uncertainty: Concrete code values are an implementation detail; the normative content is name-independence + per-shape distinctness.

rules.title: Struct identity recurses through substituted field types
rules.statement: Structural identity of a struct type S<A...> mixes the struct shape tag, the field count, and the identity of each field type after substituting S's type-params by the concrete type-args A.... Generic struct instances thus get distinct identity per instantiation by their concrete field layouts.

rules.title: Recursive struct types terminate identity computation with a cycle marker
rules.statement: When structural identity recursion re-enters a struct type already on the current walk path (recursive/self-referential types), the recursion is cut with a fixed marker rather than diverging; identity computation always terminates.

rules.title: Array length is part of structural identity; tuple arity too
rules.statement: [T; N] structural identity mixes the element type identity AND N. (T1,...,Tn) mixes the arity n and each element identity in order. Arrays/tuples differing only in length/arity have distinct identity.

rules.title: Raw pointers are !Send and !Sync absent an explicit impl
rules.statement: A raw pointer type *const T / *mut T does NOT auto-satisfy Send or Sync; it satisfies them only if an explicit (unsafe) impl is present for that pointer type. Matches Rust.

rules.title: &T: Send/Sync iff T: Sync
rules.statement: &T auto-satisfies Send iff T: Sync, and Sync iff T: Sync — i.e. the auto-trait obligation on &T is delegated to T: Sync for both Send and Sync. Matches Rust.

rules.title: &mut T: Send iff T: Send, Sync iff T: Sync
rules.statement: &mut T auto-satisfies the queried trait iff T satisfies that same trait (Send→T:Send, Sync→T:Sync). Matches Rust.

rules.title: Slice auto-trait delegates to element Sync; array preserves the trait
rules.statement: [T] (slice) auto-satisfies the queried trait iff T: Sync (slice behaves like &-borrowed element storage). [T; N] (array) auto-satisfies the queried trait iff T satisfies that same trait.
rules.uncertainty: Slice→Sync delegation for BOTH Send and Sync queries is inferred from the literal "Sync" argument regardless of trait_name; Rust treats [T] like &-storage.

rules.title: Tuples, structs, and enums auto-satisfy a trait iff all components do
rules.statement: A tuple/struct/enum auto-satisfies an auto-trait (Send/Sync) iff every component type satisfies it: tuple elements, (substituted) struct fields, and every enum-variant payload type. Auto-trait membership is structural over the substituted constituent types.

rules.title: An explicit impl of an auto-trait short-circuits the structural check
rules.statement: If a type has an explicit impl of the auto-trait (matched by mangled concrete name, type_str form, or unmangled base name), the type satisfies the trait unconditionally, bypassing the structural field/variant walk.

rules.title: Scalars and function types unconditionally auto-satisfy Send/Sync
rules.statement: Primitive scalar types (bool, all integer widths, f32/f64, char), integer/float literals, and function-item / function-pointer types unconditionally satisfy auto-traits (Send/Sync).

rules.title: Scalar ABI byte sizes
rules.statement: ABI size: void/never = 0; bool/u8/i8 = 1; i16/u16 = 2; i24/u24 = 3; i32/u32/f32/char = 4; i56/u56 = 7; i64/u64/f64/usize/isize/pointer/&/&mut/fnptr/fn-item/tagged-ptr = 8; i128/u128 = 16. The Writ-fabric widths I24/U24/I56/U56 occupy their narrow byte sizes (3 and 7).

rules.title: Slices, closures, trait objects, and DST refs are 16-byte fat values
rules.statement: A slice value, a closure, a trait object, and a DST reference each occupy 16 bytes (a two-word fat representation: data/pointer + metadata such as length, environment, or vtable).

rules.title: Array ABI size is element-size times length
rules.statement: sizeof([T; N]) = N * sizeof(T) (no per-element padding beyond the element's own size).

rules.title: Tuples and structs lay fields out sequentially with natural alignment, capped at 8
rules.statement: For a tuple/struct, fields are placed in declaration order; before each field the running offset is rounded up to that field's alignment, where alignment = min(field-size, 8) (treating zero-size as alignment 1). The aggregate's size is the final offset rounded up to the maximum field alignment encountered.
rules.uncertainty: Alignment is derived as min(size,8) rather than a separate per-type alignment; matches a same-as-size convention for scalars but may diverge for over-aligned types.

rules.title: Layout resolution prefers the best-matching partial specialization
rules.statement: When resolving the field layout of a struct instance S<A...>, the best-matching partial specialization (e.g. WMap<WString,V> over base WMap<K,V>) is selected and its pattern type-vars bound by matching the concrete type-args against the spec patterns; only if no spec matches is the base template used with positional type-param binding.

rules.title: Const-generic params used in value position substitute their concrete value
rules.statement: A const-generic parameter `<const N: T>` referenced in expression position is monomorphized by splicing its concrete value: a scalar/IntLit binding lowers to an integer literal of the substituted value; a WritStatic-literal binding splices the registered WritStatic literal at the use site.
rules.divergence: A1/A2 related: const-generics are real, distinct from const-eval

rules.title: Cloning a 128-bit literal preserves its high 64 bits
rules.statement: When monomorphization clones an integer literal whose value needs more than 64 bits (i128/u128), both the low and high 64-bit halves are preserved; cloning never silently truncates to 64 bits.

rules.title: An owned dyn-tail drop only fires through a fat DST reference
rules.statement: A let-bound value initialized from a field read drops as an owned dyn tail only when the (substituted) receiver type is a fat custom-DST reference (DstRef) and the projected field is an unsized dyn (UnsizedDyn, or a borrow-owning TraitObject); a thin pointer/reference receiver (sized inner, genuine Arc<&dyn>) is NOT a DST tail and its drop is a no-op.

rules.title: Custom-DST prefix field offsets use sequential aligned layout
rules.statement: For a custom-DST struct (header fields + unsized tail), a named field's byte offset is computed by the same sequential aligned-layout walk as a normal struct (offset rounded up to min(size,8) before each field); the unsized tail field, when reached, yields its aligned offset and substituted type for fat-pair projection reusing the DstRef's carried metadata.
